subject: Signal drift annotation + cost/latency join for per-route exploration
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Signal drift annotation + cost/latency join for per-route exploration

Hi team,

Customer (Acme Apps) flagged an uptick in 95th+ latency and token costs on their /generate-chat route over the last 3 days. They shared a few example requests (attached) and called out that the failures tend to be longer prompts with multi-tool invocations.

As a product ask, we need a way in Console -> Observability to: 
- surface per-route signals that mark suspected "signal drift" windows (e.g., sudden distribution shift of prompt length or reduced KV-cache hit rate)
- join those windows to token-level cost estimates and model-variant usage so Support/CS can quickly tell whether the cost spike is model selection, prompt shape, or routing policy related
- attach 1-3 exemplar requests to an annotated window and persist those links in the UI for runbook handoff

Request/proposal: can we add an "annotator" concept to the route timeline that supports:
1) a boolean drift flag + numeric drift_score (0-1) computed by sampling prompt-shape features
2) compact columns: model_variant, prefix_cache_hit_rate, request_tokens, generated_tokens, estimated_token_cost_usd
3) ability to pin example requests (reference IDs) and surface them inline with stack traces/trace ids

I've attached a small sample (signal_samples.csv) and a mockup with rough UX ideas. This is intended as a minimal POC we can iterate on — main acceptance criteria: triage time for Acme's issue drops by 50% (empirically: time from alert to root-cause hypothesis).

Timing: Acme is asking for a short POC by end of next week. Is that achievable? If not, what minimal scope could we deliver?

Attachments: signal_samples.csv (csv), console-annotator-mockup.fig (Figma export), drift-screenshot.png (screenshot from Acme)

Thanks,
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal drift annotation + cost/latency join for per-route exploration

Connor — thanks for the context and the sample. A few clarifying Qs before we scope: 

1) When you say "drift score", is there an existing heuristic we can reuse (e.g., KL divergence on token-length histograms) or do you want us to implement something new?
2) How many routes do we need this for initially? Acme called out /generate-chat but if we make this generic the data ingest costs could increase quickly.
3) Retention: what retention window do we need for annotated examples? 7 days should be fine for incidents but we may need 30+ days for billing investigations.

Product priority: this is useful for customer-facing triage. If we aim for a POC, acceptance criteria should include an attachment workflow (pinning example requests) and a small query UI that joins to per-token cost. We should also surface an easy export for audit (CSV or .ndjson).

I'll draft acceptance criteria and propose a 3-step MVP: sample tagging + join pipeline (backend), small timeline UX (Console), and an export + runbook template. Can Soojin scope backend cost for a 1-route POC? Happy to sync 30m today if helpful.

— Marissa
Product Manager, Console
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal drift annotation + cost/latency join for per-route exploration

Quick engineering notes from Observability team: 

We can deliver a POC for one route with the following constraints and approach: 
- Ingest: add an "annotator_tag" boolean and lightweight feature vector to the request metadata (prompt_token_count, prompt_avg_token_entropy, model_variant, kv_cache_hit) and sample 1% of requests for full join to cost pipeline. 
- Storage: pre-aggregate per-minute buckets for the route with the drift heuristics (KL on prompt length + sudden kv_cache_hit delta) to avoid full raw retention costs. For pinned examples we will store the raw request payload id (not full content) and persist up to 50 pinned ids per window.
- Join: we can join to our billing estimator (token rates by model_variant) in the offline pipeline; if we need exact invoice-level cost we will need to hit billing records which is slower. POC will use estimated_token_cost_usd.

Estimated effort: 
- Backend (ingest + aggregation + join) ~ 4 engineer-weeks (SoooJin + 1 backend).
- Console UX (timeline + pin UI + export) ~ 3 engineer-weeks (Sofia + 1 frontend).
- QA + rollout ~ 1.5 engineer-weeks.

If product narrows scope to: one route, 7-day retention for pinned examples, and sampling 1% we can get POC ready in ~3 weeks. If Acme needs end-to-end exact billing joins, add 2 weeks.

Acceptance criteria request: please provide the following so we can scope precisely:
- list of route(s) to enable (one string)
- whether sampled or full ingest for pinned examples (recommended: sampled)
- target retention for pinned examples

I'll start a spike ticket (OBS-1743) and add an initial schema proposal to the ticket.

— Soojin
Senior Software Engineer, Observability
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal drift annotation + cost/latency join for per-route exploration

Thanks — this is helpful and realistic.

For the POC with Acme:
- route: /generate-chat (only)
- sampling: 1% full ingest for enriched joins; pinned examples will be allowed via Console but capped at 50 per incident window
- retention: pinned example ids persisted for 30 days; pre-aggregated drift buckets kept for 90 days

Acceptance criteria (product):
- Console timeline shows drift windows with drift_score and compact columns (model_variant, kv_cache_hit_rate, request_tokens, generated_tokens, estimated_token_cost_usd)
- Ability to pin an example request from the timeline and export pinned list as CSV
- Backend pipeline produces per-minute buckets and exposes an API endpoint results for the timeline UI

Action items: 
- Marissa: write and share formal acceptance criteria doc + user scenarios by Thu EOD (owner)
- Soojin: open spike/implementation ticket (OBS-1743) and attach schema proposal + rough ETA (owner)
- Sofia: draft timeline UX mock and a short accessibility note (owner)
- Connor: collect 6 representative customer examples and confirm Acme is comfortable with 1% sampling; I will share examples by Fri noon (owner)

I'll schedule a 30-min working session for Fri 10:00-10:30 PT and add the Drive mock to the ticket.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-1743 (ticket created by Soojin), https://drive.google.com/mock/console-annotator-prototype (mockup)

Thanks all — looking forward to the POC.
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: signal_samples.csv, drift-screenshot.png
